question: True or false: the house front that falls around Buster Keaton in Steamboat Bill, Jr. was a lightweight prop?
answer: False. The facade was a real timber frame weighing around two tonnes by most accounts, and an open attic window was placed to pass around Keaton with only a few centimetres to spare. A light prop would have flexed and floated as it fell. Keaton stood on a marked spot and did not move.
move: When something looks too dangerous to be real, ask what faking it would cost.
trap: True, because no studio would drop a real wall on its star.
source: Meade, Buster Keaton: Cut to the Chase
reference: Meade, Buster Keaton: Cut to the Chase, HarperCollins, 1995
